problem: The chapter says every industrial use is first written in binary variables and turned into a Hamiltonian or QUBO, and that every use follows the same three stages. Option pricing is an expectation estimated by amplitude estimation, and credit/fraud uses a quantum kernel; neither is a QUBO and neither returns a bitstring to repair.
fix: State that the QUBO/Ising map applies to the optimisation problems (grid, routing, portfolio, docking, folding). Say option pricing and kernel methods use amplitude estimation or feature-map overlaps inside the same classical pipeline, not a QUBO.

problem: The text says the penalty applies 'whenever supply falls below demand', but the term λΣ(D_t−ΣP_g u_{g,t})² squares the difference and so penalises both shortage and surplus equally. A student will think only shortage is penalised.
fix: Either change the wording to 'a penalty for any mismatch between supply and demand D_t', or use λΣ_t max(0, D_t−Σ_g P_g u_{g,t})² if only shortage is to be penalised.

problem: a_g u_{g,t} is charged in every slot the generator is on. That is a fixed/no-load on-cost, not a start-up cost; a start-up cost should be charged only when u changes from 0 to 1.
fix: Introduce y_{g,t}=1 when generator g starts in slot t, and use a_g y_{g,t}; or relabel a_g as a fixed no-load cost and remove 'start-up'.

problem: With only y_g=1 if 'a ligand atom' sits in cell g, the model cannot say which ligand atom is in which cell. Bond lengths and atom-type contacts need atom-specific assignments. The phrase 'one atom per cell' is also the wrong constraint; standard constraints are one cell per atom and at most one atom per cell.
fix: Define y_{a,g}=1 if ligand atom a occupies cell g. Add one-hot penalties Σ_g y_{a,g}=1 for each atom a and at-most-one penalties for Σ_a y_{a,g}>1 in each cell. Contact energy sums over atom pairs and neighbouring cells. If a single occupancy bit per cell is intended, label it a toy occupancy model, not full docking.

problem: The sentence 'Every instance above is small enough for a laptop to simulate, tens of qubits at most' contradicts the earlier statement that a lithium–air candidate or catalyst surface needs far more qubits than today's hardware holds, and it is false for the full grid, docking and folding instances described.
fix: Say that the instances actually run on today's quantum hardware are small enough for a laptop to simulate, tens of qubits at most; the full industrial problems above need far more qubits.

problem: The claim that a portfolio QUBO without the holding-count penalty returns the empty portfolio is false. Holding nothing gives cost 0, but holding assets with positive expected return gives negative cost unless λ is very large, so the unpenalised model may hold many assets or all positive-return assets. The penalty is needed to force exactly K holdings, not to prevent an automatic empty answer.
fix: Rewrite: without the holding-count penalty the model is free to choose any number of assets; depending on λ it may hold all positive-return assets, a subset, or none. The penalty fixes the count at K.

problem: The figure says all six problems map to a Hamiltonian or QUBO, and includes Option pricing. Option pricing is handled by amplitude estimation, not by a QUBO.
fix: Change the root note/caption to 'Hamiltonian/QUBO or amplitude estimation', or replace Option pricing in this QUBO figure with a genuinely QUBO finance problem.
